I appreciate what they are trying to do, but for fucks sake NFL, get your shit together. It's not totally the referees fault. The god damn rule book has gotten so bloated, and convoluted that no one understands it all. When you hear announcers, who are often times former players, who have no clue whether a call is right or not, you have problems. Example, no one knows what constitutes a catch anymore.

I'm sure better technology and more replay angles and so forth have brought more scrutiny because it's so much easier for the average fan to examine the hell out of every play and get mad, but twenty years ago there was never endless debate over "football moves" and the like. You used the eyeball test and most of the time most of us agreed. Sometimes you'd get mad about a call, but it was very much like baseball in that refs used their discretion the way an ump does with a strike zone. Some refs might have been tighter than others but a well called game was a consistently called game not a proper interpretation of scenario 3, subpoint h, verse three of paragraph 9 of alternate situational rule CXVI.

To me the answer is replay has now been opened up, and everyone can see everything, you're not putting that back in the box - so just make everything review-able without exception. In my mind anything on any play should be able to be challenged. To avoid non-stop challenges and slow downs you limit it to still two red flags a half. If you challenge and it's over turned you keep your challenge. If the ruling on the field stands you lose your challenge as it is now. If you challenge and the ruling on the field is confirmed you lose your challenge and are charged with a delay of game penalty. To me that makes it so any key play can be given the best chance to be called correctly in entirety, but also forces a strategic use of challenges and begs as to if it's worth it to slow a game down over a close call. It also in complicated situations that are likely to be challenged gives the refs an uplink to "NY" (or wherever) were the NFL could have people basically ready to "google" the rule book, so if a ref makes a wrong call because they got the rule book wrong, that could be challenged too.

Just stop adding in new things that are challengable- make it all so.
